budget_items.what_was_said: Chair broke down the FY27 increase between the governor's proposal and the final signed budget by category: chapter 70, charter tuition reimbursement, and smart growth school reimbursement, plus school choice.
The full cherry sheet receipts increase including UGGA and VBS/elderly funds, most of which was education-coded.

budget_items.topic: State assessments/charges increase (charter and school choice sending tuition)
budget_items.what_was_said: Extra assessments the town owes the state increased, driven by rising charter school sending tuition even as school choice sending tuition fell.

budget_items.topic: Net additional state aid for FY27
budget_items.what_was_said: Subtracting the extra assessments from the gross receipts increase gives the net additional aid figure the committee is discussing spending.

budget_items.what_was_said: Covers a grounds contracted services overage.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer: maintenance salaries to maintenance overtime
budget_items.what_was_said: Covers a maintenance overtime salary overage.
Covers elementary and primary school custodian salary overages, funded from middle and high school custodian lines.
Covers police detail costs for athletic events, funded from athletic transportation.
Covers a regular transportation overage; the business manager said the line had simply been budgeted too low the prior year, and it has since been revised for FY27.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer: high school guidance salaries
budget_items.what_was_said: Covers high school guidance counselor and secretary overages tied partly to summer scheduling issues.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer: high school substitutes
budget_items.what_was_said: Covers a high school regular substitute overage.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer: high school principal/assistant principal salaries
budget_items.what_was_said: Covers a high school principal/assistant principal salary overage; the underlying line items were too low and have been corrected for FY27.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer: special education paraprofessionals and hospital tutoring
budget_items.what_was_said: Covers overages across hospital tutoring and special-education paraprofessional lines at several schools, attributed to a staff leave of absence.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer: superintendent general supplies
budget_items.what_was_said: Covers a general supplies overage, funded from the dues and meetings line after the superintendent did not use her full allotted travel/dues budget.
Business manager reported total expenses came in at about 100.2% of budget; salary figures were still being finalized but expected to come in close to 100% with a small excess.
Referencing an earlier-year budget overage of roughly $600,000, about 2.5% of the total budget, that the district had to give back; this year's overage is expected to be smaller.
Warrants going out were noted before moving to donations.
LEAF's first year of fundraising is dispersing six grants to district programs (sound system, STEM kits, magazine subscriptions, etc.), totaling the figure heard.
Band boosters donated funds for color guard uniforms/gloves and to fund the middle school jazz band stipend.
Boosters will fund two buses for one-way transportation to away games for football and cheerleading, split into three separate donations to preserve some treasury funds.
State earmark funding to purchase 10-passenger vans for smaller programs was finalized and the vans have been ordered.
Secured for FY27 to upgrade system/technology infrastructure; a spending plan is being developed with tech and buildings/grounds departments.
Title 2 and Title 4 came in roughly flat; Title 1 came in far higher than the $96,000 originally expected, though the district said it does not know the exact reason and is not asking.

budget_items.topic: Additional one-time state budget money not being requested
budget_items.what_was_said: A member noted additional one-time money is coming through the state budget process that the district is deliberately not asking to have appropriated to schools, distinguishing it from the recurring aid increase.

budget_items.topic: FY27 warrant article amount for additional state aid
budget_items.what_was_said: Discussion of whether to request the smaller previously-voted amount, the full chapter-70-area increase, or the full total cherry sheet increase for the school department's warrant article.

Proposed use of part of the additional funding to restore a certified occupational therapy assistant position, tied to a new state restriction on 'cool-down rooms' that came with no additional state funding.
The committee voted to amend its warrant article language to request this figure (read aloud as the subtotal of all education-item increases) for the September 3rd special town meeting.

Governor Healey proposed an additional statewide per-pupil allocation from millionaire's tax revenue that would flow directly to districts without town meeting approval if passed by the legislature; Lunenburg's potential share was estimated.
New three-year MOU: FY27 3.5% increase, FY28 2.5%, FY29 2.5%, plus two added longevity steps.

budget_items.topic: Custodians' union longevity and clothing allowance
budget_items.what_was_said: Longevity pay converted from percentage to flat dollar amounts by years of service, and the clothing allowance was increased.

decisions.decision: Chair decided to re-present the cherry sheet numbers via slideshow to clarify confusion from the prior Zoom meeting.

Committee decided to submit its own school-committee warrant article for the additional state aid, rather than relying solely on Mandy Gilman's citizen petition, so the request could go through school committee process and be adjustable.
Mandy Gilman stated she will not pursue additional money through her separate citizen petition, deferring to the school committee's warrant article.
Committee agreed to take the original warrant article language, amend it, and adopt it as its own rather than creating confusion with two separate articles.
Noted that a new state commission (via Margaret Scarsdale's efforts) will study the chapter 70 formula and report back in fall FY28; committee to continue engaging with it.

Municipal Building Design Committee held an informal straw poll (not an official vote) concluding TCP likely has no remaining municipal use and should come down; committee also indicated it does not support building a new town hall given current school funding strain.
Athletic Advisory Committee restarted to help steer booster club fundraising and act as liaison between boosters and the district; membership to include at least two committee members.
Committee agreed it needs an MSBA primer/presentation for a future meeting and to begin familiarizing itself and the public with the MSBA process for Turkey Hill.

Committee will not meet in August unless a Zoom meeting is needed for additional line item transfers; next regular meeting will be the day before the September 3rd special town meeting, alongside a prior finance committee meeting.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg School Committee reviewed FY26 end-of-year line item transfers and several donations (LEAF grants, band boosters, football boosters), heard the superintendent's summer report on hiring and grants, approved a 300th-anniversary fireworks display, and — the meeting's central business — amended and voted to submit its own warrant article requesting the full additional FY27 state education aid figure for a September 3rd special ("extra special") town meeting triggered by a citizen petition. The committee also ratified a new custodians' union contract, tabled a further FY26 budget update, and heard public comment urging both an MSBA application for Turkey Hill Elementary and full use of the additional state aid for schools rather than other town needs.
